summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, encephalopathy, and depression was admitted for abdominal pain and confusion. She presented with diffuse stabbing abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, and was found to have elevated liver enzymes, a high lactate, and mild colitis on CT imaging. She was treated with IV fluids, lactulose every two hours, and a brief course of IV antibiotics, later switched to oral ciprofloxacin. Her mental status improved with lactulose, and she was deemed stable for discharge. Blood cultures showed one positive bottle for Corynebacterium, considered a contaminant. She was discharged home with services, on her baseline medications including lactulose, rifaximin, and omeprazole, with instructions to complete a 4-day course of ciprofloxacin and follow up for MRI of the liver and platelet monitoring.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C with hepatic coma
